notes.title: Notes on the data
notes.missingValues: Some values aren't published by GASTAT. They show as “N/A” here and are never treated as zero.
notes.notStated: The “Not stated” category is left out of charts, so distributions may not add up to exactly 100%.
notes.wagesByActivity: Wages by economic activity are only available from 2024.
notes.q4_2021: In Q4 2021, GASTAT's own occupation distribution doesn't add up to 100%. The numbers are shown as published.

about.title: About Marsad

vision.title: Our vision
vision.body: Saudi labor market numbers that anyone can understand, not just specialists.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.body: We turn GASTAT's quarterly tables into interactive charts in Arabic and English that you can filter and share.

goals.title: Our goals
goals.body: Find any number in seconds, see the trend over years rather than a single snapshot, and always know where a number comes from and its limits.

audience.title: Who is it for?
audience.body: Students, researchers and journalists, and anyone looking for work or planning a career who wants to understand the market through numbers.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Quick answers about Marsad and its data
faq.asideBody: Every number in Marsad is published by GASTAT, and you can always go back to the original bulletin.

whatIs.a: An interactive dashboard of Saudi labor market indicators, quarter by quarter since 2021: unemployment, employment, wages, regions and women's participation.

official.a: No. Marsad is an independent personal project, not affiliated with any government entity, but it relies entirely on official published data.

source.q: Where does the data come from?
source.a: From the Labor Market Statistics bulletin GASTAT publishes every quarter, based on the Labour Force Survey.

updates.q: How often is the data updated?
updates.a: Every quarter, after GASTAT publishes its new bulletin. A script in the project converts the Excel file into the site's data and checks the numbers.

missing.a: GASTAT didn't publish them for that period, usually because the sample was too small. We show them as not available and never as zero, so charts don't mislead.

participation.q: What does the labor force participation rate mean?
participation.a: The share of working-age people (15 and over) who are working or looking for work. People who are neither, such as students and retirees, are outside the labor force.

unemployment.q: How is the unemployment rate calculated?
unemployment.a: The share of people looking for and available for work, out of the whole labor force: the employed and the unemployed together.

what.title: What is Marsad?
what.body: Marsad is an interactive dashboard of Saudi labor market indicators, quarter by quarter: unemployment, employment, wages, regional differences and women's participation. Every page can be filtered by nationality, gender and period, and the link keeps the filters when shared.

saduStory.title: Why Al Sadu?
saduStory.body: Al Sadu is the Bedouin weaving of the Arabian Peninsula, woven by women from wool in precise geometric patterns: diamonds, triangles and lines repeating in a steady rhythm.
saduStory.whyMersad: We chose it as Marsad's identity because data is much the same: small threads, each number saying little on its own, that together weave a full picture of the labor market.
